newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 1.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Ruling party PASOK MPs react to the government's proposed move to abolish tax breaks for MPs. Prime Minister Costas Simitis's team is working on ways to deal with the expected backlash within the party. --Meanwhile, National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou hints that tax breaks on incomes over seven million drachmas will be abolished and new taxes for very high incomes. --Finance ministry refuses to be drawn on projected wage increases and new wage scale for civil servants. --Main opposition New Democracy appears to be unravelling if yesterday's meeting of party deputies is anything to go by. The intractable issue of who will lead the party is still unresolved. --The central bank's governor rings the alarm bells over the economy, stressing the repurcussions if Greece is left out of European Economic and Monetary Union. --The glory of Byzantium goes on show at New York's Metropolitan Museum. Greeks get a sneak preview of the 400 priceless icons at last night's press conference.

--The problem of drug abuse comes to the fore in the most dramatic manner as the 173rd victim of narcotics this year dies leaning into a phone booth in central Athens. --Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos bluntly rejects a proposal by foreign deputy minister Christos Rozakis to extend the moratorium on military exercises in the Aegean, saying that government policy is expressed by ministers and not by personal opinion. --Left Coalition leader Nikos Constantopoulos asks Simitis to respond in Parliament to the "central political issue" of the appointment of publisher Stavros Psyharis to governor of the autonomous monastic community of Mount Athos. --Meanwhile, Mount Athos spokesmen say there is no question of Bosnian Serbs Radovan Karadzic and Ratko Mladic - currently wanted on war crimes charges - seeking refuge in the sanctuary, as reported recently.

--The government has adopted proposals for the taxation of state titles and large real estate holdings and finance ministry services are now working on the details. Tax exemption threshold and tax brackets are now on the table for discussion.

--New Democracy's embattled leader Miltiades Evert loses the support of two of his loyal lieutenants. Persistent leadership challenger George Souflias says ND lost "elections which could not be lost" in September. --Public Adminstration Minister Alekos Papadopoulos announces the hiring of 2,000 for municipalities.
--Former leader of the 1967 colonel's dictatorship George Papadopoulos fights for his life under guard in hospital. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
